segments.contextBefore: Access iCloud from macOS guest virtual machines.
segments.contextAfter: In macOS 15 and later, Virtualization supports access to iCloud accounts and resources when running macOS in a virtual machine (VM) on Apple silicon.

segments.source: In macOS 15 and later, Virtualization supports access to iCloud accounts and resources when running macOS in a virtual machine (VM) on Apple silicon.
segments.normalizedSource: In macOS 15 and later, Virtualization supports access to iCloud accounts and resources when running macOS in a virtual machine (VM) on Apple silicon.
segments.contextBefore: Overview
segments.contextAfter: When you create a VM in macOS 15 from a macOS 15 software image (an `.ipsw` file) using a [`VZMacHardwareModel`](vzmachardwaremodel.md) that you obtain from a [`VZMacOSRestoreImage`](vzmacosrestoreimage.md), Virtualization configures an identity for the VM that it derives from security information in the host’s Secure Enclave.
